title: Tensor and mixed coherence of objectwise normalized fibre maps
statement: Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, and a coherent continuous rational realization family $R$. Use the separated finite-type $k$-bases, their actual localized rational hearts and scalar functors, normalized geometric fibres and pullback data of [def-per-adic-fibre-comparison-data], [def-per-adic-fibre-coherence-data], [def-per-adic-normalized-fibre-data] and [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-pullback], and the actual finite scalar quotients and reduction-cone maps of [def-zl-normalized-adic-fibre-limit-data]. Given a normalized fibre family $\omega$, its normalized pullback $\alpha$, and objectwise scalar components $d$ [def-per-scalar-fibre-component-data], the fixed scalar identity and scalar composition equations and the mixed equation with $\alpha$ hold: ScalarFibreCoherence $\ell\,R\,\omega\,\alpha\,d$. The underlying heart maps are the componentwise restrictions of the actual raw unit, associator and mixed map. This asserts only equations for given components; it supplies neither their existence nor their naturality.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), Proposition 6.8.14, Remark 6.8.15; scalar fibre construction and tensor normalization

proof.text: At finite quotient level the identity removes the coefficient 1, and both successive-extension routes multiply the same two scalar coefficients. Finite stalk scalar coherence and realization scalar unit/tower coherence identify these routes with the specified raw comparisons. Their full-heart restrictions are scalarHeartUnit and scalarHeartComp.

For the mixed square the pullback germ formula takes the pulled section germ to its original germ. Scalar extension before or after does the same on every tensor generator. Realization mixed coherence identifies the raw heart comparison with scalarHeartMixed. Pass the equalities through quotient projections, inverse limits and the normalized inverse completion map. Localizing preserves them, and rational pure tensors span each fibre. The universal local normalizations identify these equations with the original fibres and the given normalized alpha.
